question: Your team will replace the payments_client module that the backend uses behind the process_refund MCP tool of the customer support agent. Before the change, you use Claude Code to find every file in the backend that imports payments_client. The backend has several hundred Python files in many directories, and the file names do not show which files use the module. Which built-in tool choice is the most effective for this search?

options.text: Use Write to add a logging line to the payments_client module, then run the agent and record which modules load it.
options.reason: Write is for full file operations, not for searching. Grep finds the import statements in the file contents directly, without changing any code.

options.text: Use Grep to search the file contents across the backend for the import statement of the payments_client module.
options.reason: Grep is the built-in tool for content search, and the guide names import statements as a typical pattern that Grep finds in file contents.

options.text: Use Glob with the pattern **/*.py to list the Python files, because the returned file paths show which files import the module.
options.reason: Glob matches file paths by name or extension patterns. It does not search file contents, so the paths say nothing about import statements.

options.text: Use Read on the payments_client module itself, because the contents of that one file list every module that imports it.
options.reason: Read loads the full contents of a file. The import statements are in the files that use the module, so a content search across the codebase with Grep is needed.
